title: Temporal cliques admit linear spanners
abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the theorem that every temporal clique on n vertices admits a temporal spanner with at most 7n edges. A temporal clique is the complete graph on a finite vertex set whose edges carry natural-number time labels, locally injective (two edges sharing an endpoint have distinct labels); a temporal spanner is a set of edges in which every vertex reaches every other one by a journey with non-decreasing labels. The result and its proof are due to Júlia Baligács (arXiv:2606.05156, 2026): the dismountability of Carnevale, Casteigts and Corsini (SAND 2025) reduces cliques to extremally matched bi-cliques, which are then covered by simple and extended stars. The compared statements give the explicit bound 7n and the asymptotic O(n) form with a bound function chosen uniformly for all cliques. They use the same definitions as the registered O(n log n) entry of the same repository. The work is supervised by Arnaud Casteigts and Karine Altisen.
